emergencyNumber: 320-2221 (Pohnpei police), 320-2213 (Pohnpei hospital). Each state has its own numbers.
healthcareSystem: Very limited public healthcare. Each of the four states (Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae) has a state hospital. Pohnpei State Hospital is the largest. Outer islands have basic dispensaries only. As a US Compact of Free Association state, referral programs send patients to Guam, Manila, or Hawaii.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is basic. State hospitals handle routine care and basic emergencies. Equipment is limited and specialist care is largely unavailable. English is the official language and spoken by medical staff. Serious conditions require evacuation to Guam or Manila.
pharmacyHours: Hospital pharmacies open 8am-5pm weekdays. Very few private pharmacies. No pharmacies on outer islands.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacy options are extremely limited — mostly hospital pharmacies. Stock is unreliable. Bring all needed medications from home. English is spoken. Some basic medications available at local stores.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is minimal. Medication availability is the main barrier. English documentation accepted. US prescriptions may be recognized due to Compact of Free Association relationship.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications in English. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring generous extra supplies — outer islands have zero pharmacy access.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation is essential. Evacuation to Guam or Manila can cost $30,000-100,000+. Ensure coverage includes remote island travel and dive-related injuries.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Dengue fever is present. No malaria risk on main islands.

waterNotes: Municipal water systems vary by state and are not reliably safe. Use bottled or boiled water for drinking. Rainwater catchment is common on outer islands. Hotels and resorts generally provide safe water.
foodSafetyTips: Eat freshly cooked food. Fish and seafood are dietary staples and generally safe when fresh. Be cautious with reef fish due to ciguatera risk — ask locals about safe species. Breadfruit, taro, and bananas are safe staples. Limited refrigeration on outer islands.
medicalTourismNote: Micronesia is not a medical tourism destination. Patients needing specialist care are referred to Guam, Manila (Philippines), or Honolulu (Hawaii) through government referral programs.
metaDescription: Health guide for Micronesia: emergency contacts, pharmacy tips, vaccinations, water safety, and medical evacuation to Guam.

hospitals.name: Pohnpei State Hospital
hospitals.notes: Largest hospital in FSM. Emergency department. English spoken. Basic diagnostic capability. Some visiting specialists.

hospitals.name: Chuuk State Hospital
hospitals.notes: State hospital serving Chuuk lagoon area. Very basic facilities. Popular with WWII wreck divers — limited dive emergency capability.

hospitals.name: Yap State Hospital
hospitals.notes: Small state hospital. Basic emergency care. English spoken.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. Basic dental services at state hospitals.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is basic — primarily extractions and emergency work. No specialist orthodontic or cosmetic dental care.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, visit the nearest state hospital. Complex dental work requires evacuation to Guam.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited mental health professionals across all states
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are minimal. Some counseling available through hospitals and community programs. Consider telehealth services.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited across all four states.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: State hospitals have basic but limited accessibility features.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads vary from paved (main islands) to dirt tracks.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility needs should plan carefully. Inter-island travel by boat or small plane is not accessible. Arrange assistance well in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing at state hospitals.
covidStatus.notes: COVID treatment capacity is limited across all states.

insuranceClaimProcess: Obtain itemized receipts from the hospital. Cash payment typically expected. Save all documentation for insurance claims. Contact your insurer's assistance line immediately for evacuation authorization.

commonCosts.note: US dollars are the official currency. Costs are moderate. Public hospital fees are subsidized. Payment expected at time of service.

medicalEvacuation.note: Evacuation to Guam is the fastest option for Yap, Chuuk, and Pohnpei. Manila is an alternative for longer-term specialist care. Commercial flights are limited — air ambulance may be necessary for critical cases.
